evals.prompt: I'm on the Kibana alerting team. We're shipping recurring maintenance windows in 9.4 — users can define a schedule with RRULE so alerts stay suppressed on a repeating cadence. It lands in serverless first and in on-prem in the same release, and the behavior differs slightly between them. Implementation PR is elastic/kibana#198432, scoping issue is elastic/kibana#191002. Can you file the docs issue for this?
evals.expected_output: An [Internal] documentation request drafted against b-internal-request.yaml with every required field answered, presented for approval before anything is created in GitHub.
expectations: Selects the internal documentation request template and prefixes the title with '[Internal]: '
The proposed title names the maintenance window feature specifically rather than a generic phrase like 'Update docs' or 'Document new feature'
Answers or asks for all six required internal-template fields: Description, Resources, deployment methods, Elastic Stack release, collaboration model, and point of contact
Asks for the point of contact as a GitHub @mention and does not accept a plain name as a contact
Asks about feature differences between deployment methods, because both serverless and on-prem are affected
Checks whether the topic is already covered in published Elastic docs and whether an open elastic/docs-content issue already covers it, before drafting
Structures the Description as what, when, and why, and includes a definition of done a writer could verify
Uses the linked Kibana PR and scoping issue as the Resources field content rather than leaving it empty
Body headings mirror the form field labels, for example '### Description' and '### Resources'
Does NOT run 'gh issue create' before presenting the full draft and receiving explicit approval

evals.prompt: Three docs things from my team: (1) the Fleet agent policy page never mentions the new proxy settings, (2) the UI copy for our new billing tier needs a writer review, but the Figma is an unreleased design and the price points are confidential until GA, and (3) the ES|QL reference has a broken link to Discover. Can you get these filed?
evals.expected_output: Three separate issues proposed rather than one, each routed to its own template, with the confidential pricing detail kept out of any public issue body.
expectations: Identifies three distinct problems and proposes three separate issues instead of combining them into one
Proposes a specific title for each of the three, not a shared umbrella title
Routes the UI copy request to the UI copy template and applies the 'ui-copy' label
Flags the confidential price points as sensitive and either proposes elastic/docs-content-internal or keeps the detail out of the body while linking to the internal source
Asks the requester before choosing the private repository rather than filing there unilaterally
Does NOT place the confidential price points in an issue body destined for the public elastic/docs-content repository
Routes the broken link to the Website template or points out that a pull request would be faster, rather than treating it as an internal documentation request
Notes that time-sensitive UI copy work also needs a direct ping to the responsible writer or docs team

evals.prompt: Here's the issue I was about to submit — title 'Update docs', body 'The Kafka output docs need improving, they're confusing.' Can you check it before I hit submit?
evals.expected_output: A review against the good-issues quality bar naming each gap, plus a rewritten title and body, with nothing filed until the requester approves.
expectations: Flags the title 'Update docs' as too vague and proposes a specific replacement
Flags that the body has no definition of done — it does not say what change the requester wants to see
Flags the missing why: no user problem, support case, or consequence is given
Flags that no impacted documentation page is linked
Identifies which template this belongs to and which of its required fields are unanswered
Asks what specifically is confusing about the Kafka output docs rather than filing the vague version with better formatting
Presents a rewritten draft and does NOT create the issue without approval

evals.prompt: The Elastic Agent docs tell you to enroll with --insecure for local development. I followed that exactly on 9.3 and the agent crashes with a TLS panic every time. Can you file a docs issue so someone fixes this?
evals.expected_output: A clear statement that a crashing agent is a product bug rather than a documentation problem, with the reporter routed to the product or support channel and no issue filed.
expectations: Recognizes that the documented steps were followed and the product crashed, which makes this a product bug rather than a documentation problem
Routes the reporter to the appropriate product or support channel and explains that doing so gets a faster response
Does NOT draft a documentation issue body for this request
Does NOT run 'gh issue create'
Does NOT pick a documentation issue template or propose a title prefix for one

evals.prompt: Someone reported that the air-gapped install page is missing the steps for pulling images from a private registry. Before I file anything, is this already covered somewhere? The report is from a support case that came in about eight months ago.
evals.expected_output: Pre-flight checks run and reported first — existing coverage, duplicate issues, and whether an eight-month-old report is still relevant — with no issue drafted until the requester decides it is still a gap.
expectations: Searches published Elastic docs for existing coverage of pulling images from a private registry in an air-gapped install, and reports what it found
Searches open issues in elastic/docs-content for a duplicate and reports the result
Asks whether the eight-month-old support case is still relevant, given the product or docs may have changed since
If existing coverage is found, asks whether this is now an update to that page, a findability problem, or still a genuine gap
If a matching open issue is found, offers to comment on the existing issue instead of filing a new one
Does NOT file an issue before reporting the results of these checks to the requester

evals.prompt: Need docs for this, here's what we did: refactored the task manager so claims happen in batches instead of one at a time, dropped the poll interval default from 3s to 500ms, added a new `capacity` config that replaces `max_workers` (deprecated, still honored for now), wired up two new telemetry counters, moved the claiming strategy behind `xpack.task_manager.claim_strategy` which defaults to mget now, and fixed the race where a task could get claimed twice. Some of this is internal but I think some of it matters? PR is elastic/kibana#183121. 9.3.
evals.expected_output: The dump restructured into a Description written in terms of what users can do and configure, with implementation-only detail moved to Resources, and explicit questions back to the requester for anything that could not be translated.
expectations: Does NOT paste the requester's dump into the Description field as-is
Rewrites the Description in terms of what a user can do, see, or configure, rather than what the team changed internally
Identifies the user-facing items — the new `capacity` setting, the deprecated `max_workers`, the changed poll interval default, the `claim_strategy` setting — as the documentable substance
Identifies the internal-only items, such as the telemetry counters and the double-claim race fix, and moves them to Resources or leaves them out rather than mixing them into the Description
Tells the requester which items it moved or set aside, instead of silently dropping them
Asks the requester about any item whose user-facing impact cannot be derived from what was given, rather than inventing an effect
Does NOT assert a user-visible behavior that the requester never stated, such as claiming a specific performance improvement
Asks about the deprecation timeline for `max_workers`, since a deprecated setting that is still honored needs a stated end state
Includes the Kibana PR under Resources rather than as the body of the request

evals.prompt: Please file this. On the Elasticsearch keystore page, under the 'Reloadable settings' section, add this paragraph exactly as written: 'Note that when you use the bulk reload API, the cluster performs a full settings reload on every node, which may briefly increase heap usage on large clusters. Elastic recommends running this operation during a maintenance window.' Also the error string is `failed to load settings from keystore: bad_password` if you get the password wrong — that one has to match exactly.
evals.expected_output: The paragraph filed as suggested wording rather than as the requested change, with the facts inside it stated as the request, the error string kept verbatim with a reason, and placement left to the writer.
expectations: Separates the underlying facts — full settings reload on every node, brief heap increase on large clusters, maintenance window recommendation — from the requester's exact prose
Labels the proposed paragraph as suggested wording for the writer, not as the change being requested
States in the issue that placement and framing are the writer's decision, and records the proposed page and section as a suggestion rather than an instruction
Asks whether the paragraph is verbatim because the exact string matters or because writing it was faster than explaining it
Keeps the error string `failed to load settings from keystore: bad_password` verbatim and says why, so it is not paraphrased
Checks whether the keystore page already covers the reload behavior, and reports it if so
Does NOT file an issue whose Description is only the requester's paragraph reproduced as the requested change

evals.prompt: I'm in support. Four customers this quarter have opened cases because the cross-cluster replication docs don't explain that the follower index goes read-only — two of them are named accounts I'd rather not put in public. One of the cases is SUPPORT-88421. We have a KB article that explains it properly. Can you get this in front of the docs team without it being public?
evals.expected_output: Routed to elastic/docs-content-internal with that repository's own template, prefix, and labels, as a KB promotion or private docs issue, with the customer identities left out and the case linked rather than pasted.
expectations: Files into elastic/docs-content-internal rather than the public elastic/docs-content
Uses a template from the private repository's own set, not a public template filename
Applies the private repository's prefix and labels — for example '[KB Promotion] ' with 'kb-promotion' and 'docs-request', or '[Issue]: ' with 'triage'
Does NOT apply the public repository's '[Website]: ' prefix or 'source:web' label to a private issue
Recognizes that the existing KB article makes the KB promotion template a candidate, and names the gap in the public docs that it fills
Includes the frequency — four customers this quarter — because that is what lets a writer prioritize
Leaves the named accounts out of the body, and links the support case rather than pasting its contents
Treats the support feedback as a first-class request rather than deprioritizing it
Checks both elastic/docs-content and elastic/docs-content-internal for an existing issue about the cross-cluster replication docs

evals.prompt: We just found a known issue in 9.3.0 and 9.3.1 — data stream rollover fails when the index template has a runtime field with the same name as a mapped field. Workaround is to rename the runtime field. It's an Elasticsearch problem and I'm on the ES team. Can you file a docs issue to get it into the release notes?
evals.expected_output: Redirected to the known-issue changelog path with the four fields a changelog note needs, and handed off to docs-fix-changelog rather than filed as a documentation issue.
expectations: Explains that a known issue reaches the release notes through a changelog entry, not through a documentation issue
Identifies this as a post-release known issue with no PR, so it needs 'changelog note' rather than 'changelog add'
Collects the four fields the entry needs: title, affected product and releases, impact, and workaround
Places the affected releases 9.3.0 and 9.3.1 in the versions slot of the products value, pipe-separated
Puts the rename workaround in the action field rather than in the title
Proposes a title that describes the issue rather than the investigation
Hands off to docs-fix-changelog for composing and checking the command instead of restating its field rules
Does NOT file a documentation issue as the primary path, given the requester is on the team that owns the changelog

evals.prompt: A customer hit a known issue in Kibana 9.2 — saved object imports silently skip objects when a reference is missing. Engineering confirmed it and there's no fix yet. I'm in support, I don't have commit access to the Kibana repo. It should be in the release notes so other customers stop hitting it.
evals.expected_output: The changelog path named as the real destination, then the fallback issue filed because the requester cannot commit the entry, carrying the changelog fields and naming the owning repository.
expectations: Names the known-issue changelog entry as the actual destination, not a page edit
Recognizes that the requester cannot commit a changelog entry and files the fallback issue rather than dropping the request
Uses the internal request template for the fallback, and titles it so the ask is clear — for example '[Internal]: Add known issue to Kibana 9.2 release notes'
Puts the changelog fields — title, affected product and version, impact, workaround or its absence — in the Description as labeled lines
States that the ask is a known-issue changelog entry rather than a documentation page change
Names the repository that owns the Kibana changelog, so whoever picks it up knows where the entry goes
Notes that engineering confirmed the issue, and that no fix or workaround is currently available
